## Purpose and Workspace
ast-grep is a Rust workspace for structural code search, linting, and rewriting. It parses source with tree-sitter, matches AST-shaped code patterns (including metavariables), and can report or transform matches. The principal user entry point is the `sg` CLI; the same engine is exposed to Node.js, Python, WebAssembly, and LSP consumers. Workspace composition is rooted at `Cargo.toml`.

## CLI Orchestration
The executable command surface is defined by `crates/cli/src/main.rs`, with reusable command logic in `crates/cli/src/lib.rs`. CLI commands dispatch search/run, scan configured rules, rewrite/fix, verification, outline extraction, language-server startup, and project creation. `crates/cli/src/run.rs` handles direct pattern execution; `crates/cli/src/scan.rs` drives rule-based repository scanning; `crates/cli/src/lsp.rs` bridges CLI invocation to the LSP crate.

## Parsing and Language Boundary
The core operates over language-neutral AST abstractions while tree-sitter supplies concrete parsers and traversal. `crates/core/src/language.rs` defines the language-facing boundary, `crates/core/src/tree_sitter/mod.rs` adapts tree-sitter, and `crates/core/src/node.rs` represents source nodes. Built-in grammar registrations live in `crates/language/src/lib.rs` and per-language modules such as `crates/language/src/rust.rs`; `crates/dynamic/src/custom_lang.rs` supports externally registered/custom languages.

## Structural Matching and Rewriting Engine
Pattern source is parsed into ASTs, matched against target trees, then optionally rendered into replacements. Matching semantics—including node kind, pattern, textual constraints, metavariables, and strictness—are concentrated in `crates/core/src/matcher.rs`, `crates/core/src/match_tree/mod.rs`, and `crates/core/src/meta_var.rs`. Rewrites cross an important safety boundary: matching produces captures and source ranges; replacement generation applies templates/structural edits via `crates/core/src/replacer.rs` and `crates/core/src/ops.rs`.

## YAML Rule Configuration
The configuration crate turns declarative rules into executable matcher/rewrite behavior. Rule schemas cover relational and referential constraints, selector/range behavior, stopping conditions, environment deserialization, fixes, and transforms. Central paths are `crates/config/src/rule_config.rs`, `crates/config/src/rule_core.rs`, and `crates/config/src/rule/mod.rs`. Configured scan flow therefore is: discover/load YAML → deserialize and validate rule definitions → compile matcher constraints → scan files → report or apply fixes. Generated/distributed JSON schemas are under `schemas/rule.json` and language-specific schema files.

## Output, Repository Processing, and Analysis Features
CLI scanning coordinates file selection, parallel work, diagnostics, and output formatting. Results are emitted as colored terminal text, JSON, interactive output, or cloud-oriented output through `crates/cli/src/print/mod.rs`, `crates/cli/src/print/json_print.rs`, and `crates/cli/src/utils/worker.rs`. The separate outline subsystem extracts code structure using default language rules: `crates/outline/src/extractor.rs`, `crates/outline/src/combined_extractor.rs`, and YAML defaults in `crates/outline/src/default_rules/`.

## Integration Runtimes and Distribution
Native CLI builds target Rust-supported platforms and are packaged for npm and PyPI. Node native bindings are in `crates/napi/src/lib.rs`, with platform npm packages under `crates/napi/npm/`; Python bindings use PyO3 via `crates/pyo3/src/lib.rs`; browser/JS WebAssembly bindings are in `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs`. Language-server functionality is its own library at `crates/lsp/src/lib.rs`. CI workflows build and publish N-API, PyO3/PyPI, WASM, and releases in `.github/workflows/`.
